question.text: A hole is drilled in a metal sheet. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, the diameter of hole is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. When the sheet is heated to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>177</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, the change in the diameter of hole is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> . The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> will be _____, if coefficient of linear expansion of the metal is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mo>∘</mo></mmultiscripts></math>

solution.text:
Expansion of hole will be similar to that of an imaginary disc.

Let diameter be d0 at 27 °C and d' at 177 °C. Therefore, we can write

d'=d01+αΔT

Therefore, change in diameter will be

⇒d'-d0=5×1.6×10-5×177-27

=12×10-3 cm

Hence, required value of d=12.
